Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-01-09 15:00 PST
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Rosa Martinez (Redwood CSM); Marissa Kwan (BluePoint Head of Platform), Devon Ortiz (BluePoint Partnerships), Elliot Kim (CTO), Noah Rivers (Data Infra)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Quick partner co-sell pipeline sync. Review top 6 joint opportunities, align on technical benchmarking for one large deal, discuss security/compliance asks for enterprise pipeline (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and confirm next steps for exec intro and forecast updates.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Jordan, I'll run the partner side. Samir will cover the tech, Rosa for CSM and security.
[00:15] Devon: Hey all, thanks — Devon here. We sent the latest pipeline you had access to earlier today, right?
[00:25] Jordan: yeah sent it this morning, link's in the calendar note. real quick, we want to run through the top 6 deals and pick which ones we push for co-sell this quarter.
[00:40] Marissa: High level, BluePoint's prioritizing inference infra deals now — Platform customers asking for lower latency and private deployments. Elliot's team has a P0 with a finserv customer that needs VPC + audit logs.
[00:55] Samir: okay, that's the sort we want to validate on Dedicated. a quick clarifying q: for the finserv P0, are they expecting on-prem or just VPC/private tenancy?
[01:10] Noah: it's VPC with strict egress rules, possible on-prem if the compliance team asks. also need KMS/HSM integration and per-request audit logs.
[01:25] Rosa: we can provide our Private bundle and KMS integration — we'll share the docs after. I know SOC 2 is required too.
[01:40] Jordan: great. let's walk pipeline. Opportunity 1: "Atlas Bank" — estimate 500k ARR, timeline Q2, decision maker is infra lead. Where do we land on technical fit?
[01:55] Elliot: Atlas has heavy batch + low-latency for some recommendations. They care about cost-per-token and worst-case p95 latency.
[02:10] Samir: for p95 at 2-3s on Llama-2 style models we suggest Redwood Dedicated with optimized kernels, plus prefix KV caching. note: our KV cache sometimes gets transcribed as K-V cash, so docs call it KV.
[02:30] Marissa: curious on quantization — can you support 4-bit Qs across the stack?
[02:40] Samir: yes we support 4-bit and int8 profiles, but quality tradeoffs vary; we'll run a quick eval during benchmark. the runtime switches kernels per model and sequence length so perf changes.
[02:55] [02:55] Devon: who's usually owner on pricing for co-sell? the commission split — is that in the deck?
[03:05] Jordan: yes deck has standard partner splits, but it's flexible. I'll send the one-pager with the splits and motions.
[03:15] Noah: tech question — can you expose per-request audit logs to our SIEM via syslog/S3?
[03:25] Rosa: yes we have audit log exports, can do S3 forwarding and webhooks; we'll include examples.
[03:35] [03:35] Elliot: are there any existing references in finance for latency-sensitive customers?
[03:45] Jordan: we do, I'll share a recent benchmark with a payments customer — it's in the pipeline deck link.
[03:55] Samir: for benchmarking, ideally we run two profiles: hosted API test and Dedicated test with same model/config, measure tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, and cost per 1M tokens. we'll need a short script from BluePoint to emulate their traffic.
[04:15] Marissa: we can provide traffic profile and sample payloads.
[04:25] Samir: perfect. Action: Samir will propose a test plan.
[04:35] [04:35] Jordan: moving on, Opportunity 2: "RetailCo" — mid-market, chat-based recommender. lower compliance needs but sensitive PII. thinking hosted API with VPC NAT and token redaction.
[04:55] Devon: RetailCo wants clear price predictability — their procurement hates surprises.
[05:05] Rosa: Recommend Dedicated for predictability, or hosted with usage guards; we can set quotas and rate limits per route.
[05:20] [05:20] Marissa: any objections we've seen about model quality when quantizing? RetailCo will test with embeddings and reranking.
[05:30] Samir: embeddings are pretty stable; reranker quality depends on model family. we can run evals on their test prompts. quality regression monitoring in Redwood Optimize flags if we degrade.
[05:45] [06:00] Jordan: quick pause — any competitors in these deals?
[06:05] Devon: Anthropic and a smaller infra vendor called XenonInference popped up on Atlas.
[06:15] Jordan: noted. we'll call out differentiators: production-grade latency, routing/fallback, and cost controls via batching and caching.
[06:30] [06:30] Opportunity 3: "MediCore" — healthcare customer with data residency + high compliance. timeline Q3.
[06:50] Elliot: MediCore will likely require on-prem or strict VPC with no egress. strongly prefer on-prem.
[07:05] Rosa: Private package supports on-prem; we'll need to coordinate network and deployment schedule. also mention certs — they want SOC2 + ISO docs.
[07:25] Samir: on-prem has extra setup time; we should scope that early in POC. show them expected lead times.
[07:40] [08:00] Jordan: recap so far: Atlas (priority), RetailCo (secondary), MediCore (qualified). Next up opportunities 4-6 quick pass.
[08:15] Devon: Opportunity 4: "EdgeNet" — smaller, but could expand. EdgeNet might use Redwood hosted for early stage.
[08:30] Marissa: Opportunity 5: "LogiFlow" — internal procurement wants annual commit.
[08:40] [09:00] Jordan: Opportunity 6: "FinOpt" — this one's big, looks similar to Atlas, but decision timeline is slower — Q4.
[09:15] Samir: for the big deals we should run a joint technical bench for Atlas and FinOpt to show p95 and cost per token on the exact models they care about.
[09:30] Noah: we need a non-prod sandbox in Redwood Dedicated for the bench; can you provision a short-lived pool?
[09:40] Samir: yes we can spin up a dedicated pool for a week for benchmarking, we'll document cost.
[09:50] [09:50] Marissa: procurement question — what about data retention and deletion policies?
[10:00] Rosa: by default we do configurable retention; for private and dedicated we can set retention to zero after X days and provide deletion proofs for audits.
[10:15] Jordan: there's also SSO/SAML support — how mature is that?
[10:25] Rosa: it's supported, has RBAC and SCIM provisioning. we'll include sample configs.
[10:35] [10:35] Elliot: security team will want encryption at rest with their KMS. can Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
[10:45] Samir: yes; we integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM options). we'll include integration docs.
[10:55] Devon: good. let's discuss org-level motions — co-sell assignment; do we have a recommended routing for leads from BluePoint?
[11:05] Jordan: yes typically co-sell leads go through partner rep and AE assigned co-owner in CRM. we'll define lead scoring thresholds so both sides escalate appropriately.
[11:15] [11:15] Marissa: also want to know if Redwood offers trial credits or pilot discounts for customers coming via partners.
[11:25] Jordan: we do partner-specific pilots and credits; I'll include the standard pilot offer in the deck.
[11:35] [11:35] Devon: next, a question on SLAs for Dedicated — what are uptime and latency guarantees?
[11:45] Rosa: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime, and latency SLOs are customer-specific; we'll propose targets in the SOW and include fallback policies e.g., model variant fallback to hosted pool if Dedicated capacity is constrained.
[11:55] Samir: important to note fallback behaviors — we can route to compatible model variants, but you may see cost/latency shifts.
[12:10] [12:10] Jordan: tooling — on the console you'll see token-level cost and per-route dashboards; that helps procurement and product owners track spend.
[12:25] Noah: great. for the bench, what metrics do you expose?
[12:35] Samir: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens; we'll provide a CSV export.
[12:50] [13:00] Jordan: wrap-up section — agree we run benchmark for Atlas as priority, provision Dedicated sandbox week of 1/19, exec intro targeted 1/20, and Jordan to send the deck by 1/12.
[13:20] Devon: sounds good. can we get a stub SOW or pilot template?
[13:30] Rosa: yes, I'll attach a pilot SOW template with baseline terms.
[13:40] [13:40] Marissa: last thing — competitors: Anthropic is doing LLM-only play, XenonInference pitched on price — we should call out reliability and routing features.
[13:55] Jordan: will do. final recap of action items and owners.
[14:10] Samir: technical note — when we run the test, please include the exact model checkpoint and seq lengths to match production.
[14:25] Noah: will do.
[14:35] [14:35] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll circulate notes and the deck. expect Rosa's security pack and Samir's bench plan early next week.
[14:50] Devon: thanks, appreciate it.
[14:55] Elliot: bye all.
